Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray shows lucent streaks outlining mediastinal structures consistent with pneumomediastinum, and the absence of pleural effusion or lung opacification supports spontaneous pneumomediastinum due to alveolar rupture (Macklin effect) rather than esophageal perforation. This aligns with the clinical history of vomiting-induced barotrauma without signs of sepsis or hydropneumothorax.
